No marginal notes on this page. Reading order: running head, text column from top to bottom, then the page number.

p.i: Fuerunt causæ ex parte principis: restant causæ ex parte subditorum, quæ etiam sunt vel Ethicæ, vel Politicæ.

main_text.head: De Ethicis causis sunt Canones:
main_text.p: 1 Cum inter subditos grassantur scelera & excutitur omnis reuerentia legum, & viuitur licentiosè, in libidinib. & luxu, sequuntur mutationes.
2 Cum subditi degenerant à pristina fortitudine, & fiunt imbelles atq; effœminati, conuertuntur imperia.
main_text.head: De causis politiæ sunt hi Canones:
main_text.p: 1 Cum subditi incipiunt odisse Principes & eorum tædio affici, sequuntur mutationes; & rarò eum principem, cuius tædio afficiebantur, sequitur melior.
3 Inobedientiam & contumaciam subditorum comitatur rerum conuersio.
4 Ubi nec legibus nec magistratui honor habetur, diu salua esse resp. nequit.
main_text.head: CAP. XXVII.
De vitiis reip. minus grauibus.
main_text.p: HUcusq; de causis mutationum in principatu, siue rep. sequuntur vitiorum & corruptelarum.

page.notes: The narrow strip at the left edge shows only cut-off fragments of the facing left page (e.g. "ulo", "nta", "ficit", "inci", "rum", "den", "gno", "ditos", "ere in", "tione", "Fuē"). These are too fragmentary to read reliably, so they are not transcribed. The initial "H" is a large drop cap joined to "Ucusq;" (printed "Vcusq;"). The running head is printed "LIBER L" in small capitals. The caput number XXVII is printed as a Roman numeral. Printed "Vide" and "Vbi" were kept with the capital V as printed in the Ubi line, normalised to U per the vowel rule where it begins a word.
